boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented UCLA customs spanning songs, rivalry rituals, campus landmarks and student traditions.

cards.title: Lead the UCLA 8 Clap
cards.subtitle: UCLA athletics cheer
cards.notes: Learn the letter-and-clap cadence before a game, then join only when event leaders and the crowd begin it.
cards.evidence_claim: UCLA Marching Band history states that the 8 Clap was introduced as a UCLA cheer in 1948.
cards.access_notes: Use at an organized UCLA athletics event or spirit gathering.

cards.title: Stretch the Long “L”
cards.subtitle: UCLA 8 Clap variation
cards.notes: Listen for the extended “L” in the 8 Clap and follow the cadence rather than trying to start it alone.
cards.short_summary: A later twist on UCLA’s signature cheer.
cards.evidence_claim: UCLA Marching Band history says Annamarie Nieto began extending the “L” in 1990 and that the practice spread through the band.
cards.access_notes: Typically encountered with the 8 Clap at UCLA spirit events.

cards.title: Spot the Victory Bell
cards.subtitle: UCLA–USC football trophy
cards.notes: See the bell in an official display or game context, and read its rivalry history without touching restricted athletics property.
cards.short_summary: The annual football rivalry’s traveling trophy.
cards.evidence_claim: UCLA Alumni documents that the Victory Bell became the permanent trophy awarded to the winner of the UCLA–USC football game.
cards.access_notes: Follow event and athletics staff directions around trophy displays.

cards.title: See the Bruin Bear “Hibernate”
cards.subtitle: Westwood Plaza rivalry-week ritual
cards.notes: During the UCLA–USC game week, look for the protected statue and its hibernation sign from public walkways.
cards.short_summary: A protective rivalry-week covering for the Bruin Bear.
cards.evidence_claim: UCLA Alumni states that the Bruin in Westwood Plaza is covered with a tarp and a “Bruin Bear is hibernating” sign before the big game.
cards.access_notes: View from public areas; do not interfere with the protective covering.

cards.title: Take in Spring Sing
cards.subtitle: Annual student music, dance and comedy showcase
cards.notes: Watch for the annual program and enjoy the student performances; obtain admission only through the event’s official channel.
cards.evidence_claim: UCLA Alumni describes Spring Sing as an annual concert dating to 1945 featuring student song, dance and sketch comedy.
cards.access_notes: Admission and venue vary by year; confirm details on the official event listing.

cards.title: Photograph the Inverted Fountain
cards.subtitle: Franz Hall landmark and Bruinization custom
cards.notes: Photograph the fountain from the plaza and appreciate the documented start-to-graduation custom; do not enter the water.
cards.short_summary: A fountain associated with UCLA’s Bruintization tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: Daily Bruin reports that new students touch the Inverted Fountain when “Bruintized” and traditionally avoid it again until completing their last final.
cards.access_notes: Observe from public paths; fountain entry is not encouraged.

cards.title: Visit the Bruin Bear Before Finals
cards.subtitle: Ackerman Union area
cards.notes: Find the bronze bear from the public plaza and take a photo; respect the statue and surrounding pedestrian traffic.
cards.short_summary: A finals-time good-luck gesture at the Bruin Bear.
cards.evidence_claim: Daily Bruin documents the custom of UCLA students rubbing the Bruin Bear’s paw for good luck during midterms and finals.
cards.access_notes: The statue is publicly viewable except when protected during UCLA–USC rivalry week.

cards.entity_name: “Hail to the Hills of Westwood” V Gesture
cards.title: Raise a V for the Alma Mater
cards.subtitle: Post-sporting-event song custom
cards.notes: Learn the alma mater before an event and raise outstretched fingers in a V above your head while it is sung.
cards.short_summary: A victory-sign gesture paired with UCLA’s alma mater.
cards.evidence_claim: UCLA Alumni says Bruins traditionally hold a V high over their heads while singing “Hail to the Hills of Westwood” after sporting events.
cards.access_notes: Most relevant after a UCLA sporting event when the alma mater is performed.

cards.entity_name: “By the Old Pacific’s Rolling Waters” Pregame Performance
cards.title: Listen for “By” at Pregame
cards.subtitle: UCLA football pregame tradition
cards.notes: Arrive for football pregame and listen for the song’s performance by the Marching Band and Cheer Squad.
cards.short_summary: UCLA’s former main fight song remains part of football pregame.
cards.evidence_claim: UCLA Alumni states that “By the Old Pacific’s Rolling Waters” is played by the UCLA Marching Band and performed to by the Cheer Squad at every football pregame.
cards.access_notes: Requires access to the football event for the pregame performance.

cards.title: Work Toward Traditions Keeper
cards.subtitle: UCLA Alumni recognition program
cards.notes: Use the official program information to identify eligible traditions and complete them over time if you are a participating student.
cards.short_summary: A UCLA program recognizing completion of campus traditions.
cards.evidence_claim: UCLA Alumni says students completing a required number of UCLA traditions can receive a True Bruin Traditions Keeper medal in their final senior-quarter ceremony.
cards.access_notes: Eligibility, completion thresholds and ceremony details are administered by UCLA Alumni.
